title: Account deletion in Sefaria removes the user's social data

tasks.title: Signed user-deleted webhook with idempotent deletion and a tombstone
Staff purge-user command for a lost webhook

acs.text: WHEN `POST /api/v1/internal/user-deleted` arrives without an `X-Sefaria-Signature` header equal to `sha256=` followed by the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body keyed with `USER_DELETED_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, THE SYSTEM SHALL respond 401 with `webhook.bad_signature` and change nothing.
scenarios: A webhook without a valid signature is refused

acs.text: WHEN a correctly signed `user.deleted` event for user U arrives THE SYSTEM SHALL, in one transaction, delete U's memberships, the rooms U owns (with their memberships), the shiurim U teaches, the recordings U owns and U's display cache entry, record a tombstone (user id, time, event id) and the event id as received, and respond 200 with `{"status":"processed"}`; a test seeds every table with rows for U and for another user, walks the database schema, and finds no value equal to U's id in any column of any table except the tombstone, while the other user's rows remain.
scenarios: A signed deletion removes the user's rows from every table

acs.text: WHEN an event id that was already received arrives again THE SYSTEM SHALL respond 200 with `{"status":"duplicate"}` and change nothing.
WHEN a user with a tombstone calls a protected route with an otherwise valid token THE SYSTEM SHALL respond 401 with `auth.user_deleted` and not run the handler.
scenarios: A deleted user's still-valid token is refused

acs.text: WHEN staff run `npm run purge-user -- <userId>` with the server's database configuration THE SYSTEM SHALL delete that user's data and write the tombstone exactly as the webhook does, and print how many rows it removed per table.
scenarios: Staff purge a user whose webhook was lost

acs.text: WHEN a correctly signed event of another type arrives THE SYSTEM SHALL respond 200 with `{"status":"ignored"}`, record the event id, and change no user data.
scenarios: A signed event of an unknown type is acknowledged and ignored
